run.subject: D-002
run.final_text:
The draft withholding schedule for D-002 is ready for your review as WS-R001: of the $8,000,000, $1,175,900 is withheld and $6,824,100 is paid out. I've stopped at step 10; second review and sign-off are yours. Five of the 15 lines are on the 30% default rate and nothing is held.

**Data dates for D-002.** Many of the records I relied on are dated after today (15 Oct 2026):
- The record date (15 Dec 2026) and payment date (12 Jan 2027) are both in the future.
- The upstream dividends P-009 and P-010 are dated December 2026.
- The distribution notice DOC-0202 is dated 7 Dec 2026.
- Moselle's Belgian residence record starts 1 Dec 2026.

So the investor list is not really frozen yet. It should be run again on or after the record date before you sign off.

**Totals**

| | Lines | Gross | Tax withheld | Net |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cleared at 10% treaty rate (R-02/2027.1) | 6 | 5,279,000 | 527,900 | 4,751,100 |
| Cleared at 30% statutory rate, documented (R-01) | 2 | 464,000 | 139,200 | 324,800 |
| Default rate, 30% | 5 | 1,696,000 | 508,800 | 1,187,200 |
| Not subject to withholding (US persons) | 2 | 561,000 | 0 | 561,000 |
| **Total** | 15 | **8,000,000** | **1,175,900** | **6,824,100** |

The dividend came from Orion Manufacturing Inc. (E-003) through the acquisition SPV. Nobody holds 10% of Orion's votes, so the 5% rate (R-03) applies to no one. The closest are Limpertsberg at 9.99% and Ardennes at 9.6%. Kirchberg has 10% economically but 0% of the votes, because its Class A2 units carry none.

**Lines not cleared**
- **I-011 Moselle Capital** (30% share of the Lux feeder's line), $576,000 on default. Its form F-011 still claims the Luxembourg treaty, but it has been resident in Belgium since 1 Dec 2026, and the rules in force have no US–Belgium treaty rate. The feeder's clearance CL-002 relies on F-011, yet no change case is open on it. **I recommend opening one.** Cure: a new form showing current residence.
- **I-006 Meridian Holdings I**, $240,000 on default. A change case (K-006) is open on its clearance, and its treaty claim on ownership grounds can't be tested. Meridian I and Meridian II each own 30% of the other (DOC-0106), so the ultimate owners can't be traced. The treaty assessment is recorded as undetermined, and a person needs to resolve this.
- **I-013 Echternach Pension Fund** (behind Sterling Nominees), $300,000 on default. Its form F-013 expires on 31 Dec 2026: valid on the record date but not on the payment date. If a renewed form arrives before payment, this line would qualify for 10%.
- **I-014 Client account 7731** (behind Sterling Nominees), $180,000 on default. It has no form and no recorded residence (open item MF-001).
- **I-015 Bertrange Capital**, $400,000 on default. Its clearance was withdrawn on 1 Jan 2026 and its form F-015 expired on 31 Dec 2025.

**Hold versus default rate.** The fund's limited partnership agreement (DOC-0001) is indexed but not digitised, so I couldn't read whether the fund's terms allow holding a payment. Under decision rule 10, every line that couldn't clear goes on the default rate instead of being held.

**Where sources disagree.** In both cases I used the investor register, which is the system of record:
- **Lux feeder's votes in the fund:** the register says 24%; entity management (H-005b) says 25%. On 25%, Ardennes (I-010) would have exactly 10% of Orion's votes and qualify for 5% instead of 10%, a difference of $48,000. **This one is worth checking.**
- **Atlas Co-Invest's share of the fund:** the register says 3.0%; entity management (H-006) says 3.5%. Its line is paid gross either way, but the amount would change.

**Other points**
- Two investors share the name Alpha Holdings SA. They were matched on legal entity identifier: I-008 is in Luxembourg and gets 10%; I-009 is Swiss, made no treaty claim and gets 30%.
- The schedule has one line per recipient. The feeder (I-002) is split across Ardennes, Moselle and Claire Dumont, and Sterling Nominees (I-007) across Echternach and the client account.
- The rulebook says its rules are illustrative and haven't been checked against the primary legal text.

The distribution case is K-R001.

WITH dist AS (
    SELECT d.record_dt, d.pay_dt, f.fund_code
    FROM treasury.distribution d
    JOIN treasury.counterparty cp ON cp.cp_id = d.fund_cp
    JOIN investor_register.fund f ON f.lei = cp.lei
    WHERE d.dist_id = %(distribution_id)s
), intermediary AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT t.inv_no
    FROM onboarding.tax_form t, dist
    WHERE t.is_intermediary = 'Y' AND t.form_status <> 'SUPERSEDED'
      AND t.signed_dt <= dist.pay_dt AND (t.valid_to IS NULL OR t.valid_to >= dist.pay_dt)
), payee AS (
    SELECT c.inv_no, c.commit_id, i.lei, c.inv_no IN (SELECT inv_no FROM intermediary) AS looked_through
    FROM dist
    JOIN investor_register.commitment c ON c.fund_code = dist.fund_code
         AND c.from_dt <= dist.record_dt AND (c.to_dt IS NULL OR c.to_dt >= dist.record_dt)
    JOIN investor_register.investor i ON i.inv_no = c.inv_no
), recipient AS (
    SELECT p.inv_no AS investor_no, p.inv_no AS recipient_no, 100::numeric AS share_pct, 'own account' AS basis,
           'investor_register.commitment:' || p.commit_id AS source_ref
    FROM payee p WHERE NOT p.looked_through
    UNION ALL
    SELECT p.inv_no, c.inv_no, c.unit_pct, 'investor in a flow-through fund vehicle',
           'investor_register.commitment:' || c.commit_id
    FROM payee p
    JOIN investor_register.fund f ON f.lei = p.lei
    JOIN investor_register.commitment c ON c.fund_code = f.fund_code
    CROSS JOIN dist
    WHERE p.looked_through AND c.from_dt <= dist.record_dt AND (c.to_dt IS NULL OR c.to_dt >= dist.record_dt)
    UNION ALL
    SELECT p.inv_no, o.owner_inv_no, o.pct_econ, 'beneficial owner behind a nominee',
           'onboarding.declared_owner:' || o.decl_id
    FROM payee p
    JOIN onboarding.declared_owner o ON o.owned_inv_no = p.inv_no AND o.alloc_basis = 'NOMINEE_ALLOC'
    CROSS JOIN dist
    WHERE p.looked_through AND o.from_dt <= dist.record_dt AND (o.to_dt IS NULL OR o.to_dt >= dist.record_dt)
)
SELECT r.investor_no, r.recipient_no, i.display_name AS recipient_name, r.share_pct, r.basis,
       r.recipient_no IN (SELECT inv_no FROM intermediary) AS recipient_is_intermediary, r.source_ref

result.text:
The draft withholding schedule for D-002 is ready for your review as WS-R001: of the $8,000,000, $1,175,900 is withheld and $6,824,100 is paid out. I've stopped at step 10; second review and sign-off are yours. Five of the 15 lines are on the 30% default rate and nothing is held.

**Data dates for D-002.** Many of the records I relied on are dated after today (15 Oct 2026):
- The record date (15 Dec 2026) and payment date (12 Jan 2027) are both in the future.
- The upstream dividends P-009 and P-010 are dated December 2026.
- The distribution notice DOC-0202 is dated 7 Dec 2026.
- Moselle's Belgian residence record starts 1 Dec 2026.

So the investor list is not really frozen yet. It should be run again on or after the record date before you sign off.

**Totals**

| | Lines | Gross | Tax withheld | Net |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cleared at 10% treaty rate (R-02/2027.1) | 6 | 5,279,000 | 527,900 | 4,751,100 |
| Cleared at 30% statutory rate, documented (R-01) | 2 | 464,000 | 139,200 | 324,800 |
| Default rate, 30% | 5 | 1,696,000 | 508,800 | 1,187,200 |
| Not subject to withholding (US persons) | 2 | 561,000 | 0 | 561,000 |
| **Total** | 15 | **8,000,000** | **1,175,900** | **6,824,100** |

The dividend came from Orion Manufacturing Inc. (E-003) through the acquisition SPV. Nobody holds 10% of Orion's votes, so the 5% rate (R-03) applies to no one. The closest are Limpertsberg at 9.99% and Ardennes at 9.6%. Kirchberg has 10% economically but 0% of the votes, because its Class A2 units carry none.

**Lines not cleared**
- **I-011 Moselle Capital** (30% share of the Lux feeder's line), $576,000 on default. Its form F-011 still claims the Luxembourg treaty, but it has been resident in Belgium since 1 Dec 2026, and the rules in force have no US–Belgium treaty rate. The feeder's clearance CL-002 relies on F-011, yet no change case is open on it. **I recommend opening one.** Cure: a new form showing current residence.
- **I-006 Meridian Holdings I**, $240,000 on default. A change case (K-006) is open on its clearance, and its treaty claim on ownership grounds can't be tested. Meridian I and Meridian II each own 30% of the other (DOC-0106), so the ultimate owners can't be traced. The treaty assessment is recorded as undetermined, and a person needs to resolve this.
- **I-013 Echternach Pension Fund** (behind Sterling Nominees), $300,000 on default. Its form F-013 expires on 31 Dec 2026: valid on the record date but not on the payment date. If a renewed form arrives before payment, this line would qualify for 10%.
- **I-014 Client account 7731** (behind Sterling Nominees), $180,000 on default. It has no form and no recorded residence (open item MF-001).
- **I-015 Bertrange Capital**, $400,000 on default. Its clearance was withdrawn on 1 Jan 2026 and its form F-015 expired on 31 Dec 2025.

**Hold versus default rate.** The fund's limited partnership agreement (DOC-0001) is indexed but not digitised, so I couldn't read whether the fund's terms allow holding a payment. Under decision rule 10, every line that couldn't clear goes on the default rate instead of being held.

**Where sources disagree.** In both cases I used the investor register, which is the system of record:
- **Lux feeder's votes in the fund:** the register says 24%; entity management (H-005b) says 25%. On 25%, Ardennes (I-010) would have exactly 10% of Orion's votes and qualify for 5% instead of 10%, a difference of $48,000. **This one is worth checking.**
- **Atlas Co-Invest's share of the fund:** the register says 3.0%; entity management (H-006) says 3.5%. Its line is paid gross either way, but the amount would change.

**Other points**
- Two investors share the name Alpha Holdings SA. They were matched on legal entity identifier: I-008 is in Luxembourg and gets 10%; I-009 is Swiss, made no treaty claim and gets 30%.
- The schedule has one line per recipient. The feeder (I-002) is split across Ardennes, Moselle and Claire Dumont, and Sterling Nominees (I-007) across Echternach and the client account.
- The rulebook says its rules are illustrative and haven't been checked against the primary legal text.

The distribution case is K-R001.
